What advantage does it provide, I mean? It's not like people with crooked spines can't meditate, so why try so hard to get your spine into a particular position?
Why is it important to keep your back straight during meditation?
An erect spine causes you to be more alert. I think that's all to it. You still can meditate while being slouched but it do think that you will tend to nod off in a position like this much faster.

Yeah, I would agree. It took me a while to develop strong enough back muscles. At first, sitting with my back straight for 10 minutes would hurt, but now, thanks to yoga, I can sit for a long time. I used to have the same question because I didn't want to sit with my back straight. I think it does help with concentration which in turn helps with meditation.

Yes, same for me. When starting out i would start with an erect spine and then gradually begin slouching more and more. Meditating more often gradually improved on this. I don't think i could sit for as long in a slouched position as i can with an erect spine.

You're not as likely to get uncomfortable, tired or sleepy. You stay awake and alert throughout the session. The extended spine also makes sure you're not compressing your stomach, which would make your breaths more shallow.

However, I think the most important aspect is that you don't have to focus on your position. If you learn to sit right, it gets easier to keep the same position throughout the whole session. You can even use it as a point of focus.

Keep in mind, you want to keep your spine straight, but you don't want tension. Make sure you are balanced, stable and relaxed.

My experience has been that having a straight back allows me to breathe deeply with my diaphragm much more than just my normal slouched posture. It also helps me notice the areas in my back where my muscles are extra tense, so I can focus on breathing into them more.

A trick that I've found for meditating with a straight back is to find an office chair with lumbar support for the lower back. It's not a requirement to sit cross-legged with perfect posture...using a chair with back support works just as well from my experience

It's overrated. Anything you read about in from old traditions is just not the right position for some people. But before we became a world of desk-sitters, I think a straight spine would have meant zero muscular effort, combined with a poised balance that prevents drowsiness (because you would lose stability).

Now I use a meditation bench (google it, then build one from a saw, a plank of wood, and a hot glue gun). I get a boost in alertness and ability to concentrate, compared to sitting in a chair or on the edge of my bed.
